corrections.D1_role_authority: N/A: D1 was not a defect number in the corrections list (D2-D8 only); role/state authority itself was already correctly enforced (role derived from harness/state.json + workflow.yaml, never chosen by the caller).

D2_hook_stdin_fallback_bypass.defect: .claude/settings.json PreToolUse hook was `python3 guard.py 2>/dev/null || python guard.py || exit 2`. If python3 existed and guard.py legitimately DENIED (exit 2), bash's `||` treated that as "python3 failed" and retried with `python guard.py`, but stdin had already been drained by the first invocation. The retry parsed an empty JSON event (tool_name==""), which falls through every guard.py branch to the default ALLOW -- silently converting a real DENY into an ALLOW.
D2_hook_stdin_fallback_bypass.fix: Hook now resolves a canonical interpreter ONCE via a loop over (python3, python) using `command -v` plus a functional smoke check (`"$P" -c ''`, which never touches stdin or guard.py), then execs guard.py exactly once so its exit code IS the hook's exit code. No invocation after the first one can occur under any interpreter-availability outcome.
D2_hook_stdin_fallback_bypass.extra_finding: On this dev machine, `python3` resolves via PATH to a non-functional Windows Store execution-alias stub that exits with an error without ever running a script. A naive `command -v python3 || command -v python` (checking only PATH presence, not functionality) would have picked this broken stub and made the hook deny every tool call. The functional smoke check was added specifically to catch this class of problem; init.py's `_guard_interpreter()` now runs the identical check at cold start.

D3_maintenance_global_bypass.defect: guard.py check_write() had `if maintenance and not worktree: return True, ""` -- an unconditional bypass for ANY non-worktree write path under maintenance, including app/**, front/**, or any arbitrary path outside the Harness, before protected_paths or role checks ran.
D3_maintenance_global_bypass.fix: Replaced with an explicit allowlist check against the new `harness.maintenance_allowlist` in policies.yaml (harness/**, agents/**, scripts/harness/**, tests/harness/**, runtime/**, .claude/**, .mcp.json, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, init.sh, init.ps1, environments/**, tasks/**, progress/**, evidence/**, docs/cicd/**). Paths outside that allowlist fall through to the normal protected_paths + role + state checks exactly as without maintenance.

D4_no_destructive_command_blocking.defect: policies.yaml bash.forbidden_everywhere had no patterns at all for git reset --hard, git clean -f/-fd/-xdf, git checkout -- ., git restore, rm -rf, Remove-Item -Recurse, rmdir /s, del /s. These were unblocked for any role/state, maintenance or not.
D4_no_destructive_command_blocking.fix: Added explicit forbidden_everywhere patterns for all of the above (case-insensitive match). They are checked unconditionally, before the maintenance branch, so they are blocked even under maintenance.
D4_no_destructive_command_blocking.classification: enforcement parcial + fail-closed para los patrones soportados (regex sobre el texto del comando). No se afirma cobertura total frente a shell arbitrario/ofuscado (alias, variables indirectas, encoding, binarios propios, wrappers).

D5_maintenance_audit.defect: guard.py's hook-invocation log (.harness-runtime/guard.log) never recorded whether maintenance was active for a given decision.
D5_maintenance_audit.fix: Every guard.log record now includes `maintenance_mode: true/false` and `context: "maintenance-bootstrap"|"runtime-normal"`. aws_guard.py's evidence/<task>/aws-audit.jsonl records now include `maintenance_mode` too (informational only; per D6 it never changes `mode`/`allowed`). No environment values or secrets are logged, only the boolean.

D6_maintenance_widened_aws.defect: policies.yaml had `aws.maintenance_mode: read` and `aws.maintenance_states: [IDLE, BLOCKED_HUMAN]`, and aws_guard.py's evaluate() granted AWS read access in IDLE/BLOCKED_HUMAN whenever TPI_HARNESS_MAINTENANCE=1 -- directly violating "if IDLE normally has no AWS, IDLE+maintenance must not either".
D6_maintenance_widened_aws.fix: Removed both keys from policies.yaml and the corresponding widening branch from aws_guard.py evaluate(). AWS mode now depends exclusively on role + workflow_state + environment (state_modes), unconditionally. Maintenance is recorded on the Decision/audit for traceability but never read to affect `mode` or `allowed`.

D7_secrets_shell_gap.defect: Secret-file protection relied only on the Read/Glob/Grep tool check (check_read) plus a short list of native Claude Code `Read()` permission denies. A shell command (Bash/PowerShell `cat`/`type`/`Get-Content`/etc. against .env/credentials/.aws files) went through check_command, which had no secret-file pattern at all.
fix: Native runtime denies expanded in .claude/settings.json: Read() now also denies **/.env (nested), **/*.pem, **/*.key, **/.aws/credentials, **/.aws/config (mirrors policies.yaml secret_read_deny exactly; .env.example stays readable everywhere, matching guard.py's own exception).

guard.py forbidden_everywhere gained shell-level patterns for cat/type/more/less/head/tail/Get-Content/gc against .env(.*) (excluding .example) and against 'credentials', plus a direct pattern for .aws/credentials and .aws/config paths.
D7_secrets_shell_gap.classification: enforcement parcial. No se afirma protección total contra shell arbitrario u ofuscado (variables indirectas, encoding, herramientas no listadas, wrappers, named pipes). Documentado explícitamente como limitación conocida, no como garantía.
D7_secrets_shell_gap.residual_limitation: A sufficiently indirect shell command (e.g. reading via a variable-built path, a non-listed reader binary, or base64/otherwise-encoded access) can still evade the regex-based check_command patterns. This is inherent to any denylist over free-form shell text and is called out here rather than claimed as closed.

D8_maintenance_human_only_limitation.acknowledged_as_requested: Not declared as proven. Within the same trust boundary, with arbitrary shell available, it cannot be mechanically demonstrated that TPI_HARNESS_MAINTENANCE=1 was set exclusively by a human at runtime launch (a process in that same boundary could in principle have set it before launch too).
D8_maintenance_human_only_limitation.what_is_demonstrated: M1: a CHILD shell spawned during this session cannot alter this (parent) process's environment -- confirmed via tests/harness/test_maintenance.py::test_m1_child_shell_cannot_alter_parent_environment. This is real OS-level process isolation, not a human-only guarantee.
D8_maintenance_human_only_limitation.mitigation: policies.yaml forbidden_everywhere includes a pattern denying any Bash/PowerShell command that textually contains "TPI_HARNESS_MAINTENANCE", which blocks the most direct in-session attempt to set/export/unset it from a Claude-issued shell command. This is a mitigation, not a proof.
D8_maintenance_human_only_limitation.classification: LIMITACIÓN CONOCIDA, documentada explícitamente; no se afirma enforcement real de "human-only".

root_cause.method: Reproduced the exact failure directly: spawned the exact command+args+env from .mcp.json using the real `mcp` SDK's stdio_client + ClientSession (same library Claude Code's MCP client is built on), and called session.initialize() against the live endpoint. No AWS resource operation was performed -- this is the connection handshake plus, had it succeeded, a single search_documentation call (never reached).
exact_exception_chain: botocore.errorfactory.AccessDeniedException: An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the CreateOAuth2Token operation: The refresh token has expired.
botocore.exceptions.LoginRefreshRequired: Your session has expired or credentials have changed. Please reauthenticate using 'aws login'.
mcp.shared.exceptions.McpError: Invalid request parameters  <-- this is the -32602 the session/system reports
root_cause.interpretation: The proxy must SigV4-sign every request (including `initialize`) using local credentials for profile tpi-dev. Resolving those credentials triggers botocore's OAuth2/device-token refresh, which fails because the refresh token for profile tpi-dev has expired (docs/AWS_MCP_SERVER_SETUP.md documents these `aws login` credentials as valid ~12h, renewable up to 90 days -- the renewal window has lapsed). Because credential resolution fails while the request is being prepared/signed, the initialize call that reaches (or fails to correctly reach) the backend results in the generic JSON-RPC -32602 'Invalid request parameters' response being surfaced to the client, rather than a clear authentication-error message. -32602 is therefore a MISLEADING surface symptom of an expired local credential, not a literal malformed MCP parameter, and not a bug in this repository's .mcp.json/policies.yaml/harness configuration.
root_cause.confidence: DEMOSTRADA (not a hypothesis): reproduced end-to-end with the real mcp SDK against the real command from .mcp.json; the traceback is unambiguous (AccessDeniedException on CreateOAuth2Token -> LoginRefreshRequired -> McpError 'Invalid request parameters').
not_the_cause: AWS_MCP_PROXY_PROFILES env var: confirmed correctly read and precedenced by server.py source (see configuration.profile_contract_confirmed above); ruled out.
--read-only flag / tool filtering: confirmed correctly wired in cli.py/server.py; ruled out.
Missing/broken local uvx or package install: `uvx mcp-proxy-for-aws-cli@1.6.6 --help` and module introspection both succeed; ruled out.

MCP protocol version mismatch: installed mcp 1.28.1 supports up to 2025-11-25, a current version; no evidence of a negotiation failure surfaced (the failure occurs during credential/signing, before a protocol-level response is formed).

defect_1_init_read_only.action_taken: Added regression tests (tests/harness/test_cold_start_readonly.py) proving this invariant so it cannot silently regress: git-tracked-file hashes and `git status --porcelain` are byte-identical before/after running init (both via the Python API and via the real init.py CLI subprocess), init succeeds from IDLE with no task, and a monkeypatch-based test asserts init never calls any of the four state/evidence-writing helpers. defect_2_read_only_discovery_false_posit.root_cause_confirmed_by_direct_reproduct: scripts/harness/guard.py's check_command() denies a Bash/PowerShell command when it BOTH mentions a protected-path token (e.g. 'harness/') AND matches policies.yaml's bash.protected_write_verbs regex. That regex includes a bare '>' to catch real file-write redirection (`cmd > file`), but '>' also matches harmless, non-mutating shell plumbing: fd duplication (`2>&1`, `1>&2`) and null-device discards (`2>/dev/null`, `2>$null`). Reproduced directly: `ls harness/ 2>&1`, `git status 2>&1`, and even `python scripts/harness/init.py --runtime claude 2>&1` were all DENIED before the fix, purely because of the trailing stderr redirect -- not because of any actual write.
defect_2_read_only_discovery_false_posit.fix: Added `_SAFE_REDIRECTS` (a documented regex distinguishing fd-duplication and /dev/null or $null discards from real file writes) and `_strip_safe_redirects()` in guard.py. check_command() now evaluates `protected_write_verbs` against the command with safe redirects stripped, instead of the raw command. This is a general classifier fix, not a hardcoded 'ls' exception: it improves the existing read/write distinction (protected_paths readable, not writable) that was already correctly gating on write-verb presence, rather than adding a special case for any one command name.
defect_2_read_only_discovery_false_posit.unaffected_by_design: forbidden_everywhere (AWS CLI direct, secrets, docker push/login, gh sensitive ops, boto3), the always-unconditional destructive-command patterns (git reset --hard, git clean -f*, git checkout --, git restore, rm -rf, Remove-Item -Recurse, rmdir /s, del /s), the aws_guard.py canonical-path check, and the git push/commit/merge/rebase/reset role+state gates all still run on the ORIGINAL (non-stripped) command text and are completely untouched by this fix.
defect_2_read_only_discovery_false_posit.documented: AGENTS.md '## Contrato read-only vs mutacion' section states the semantic contract (protected_path != unreadable_path; read-only discovery -- listing, git status/diff/log/ls-files, non-secret reads, non-sensitive search -- always permitted including in IDLE, even with an incidental protected-path mention or a harmless stream redirect; mutation/secrets/AWS/destructive commands remain fully gated) so any runtime's enforcement mechanism can be checked against it.
